paragraphs.title: Fortifying Jerusalem and Preparing the Records

easy.explanation: Nehemiah says that he had set up the doors after the wall was built.
easy.q: What was done after the wall was built?

answers: Hananiah the ruler of the palace
easy.explanation: Nehemiah gave Hanani and Hananiah charge over Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who was given charge over Jerusalem with Hanani?

answers: He was faithful and feared God
easy.explanation: Hananiah was described as a faithful man who feared God.

medium.explanation: The city was large, but few people lived in it, so watches were appointed.
medium.q: Why were the inhabitants appointed to watch, each one near his house?

answers: Counted or identified by family ancestry
Chosen to sing in the temple
medium.explanation: Nehemiah gathered the people so their ancestry could be recorded.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “reckoned by genealogy” mean?

answers: He appointed watches and gathered the people
medium.explanation: He organized watches and gathered the people to be recorded by genealogy.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah do after seeing that the city was large and the people were few?

answers: Security required careful control of the gates
challenge.explanation: The command shows that opening and securing the gates was part of the city’s defense.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the command not to open Jerusalem’s gates until the sun was hot?

answers: They were appointed to roles in the city and community
They built every house in the city
challenge.explanation: They were appointed as part of the organization of Jerusalem after the wall was finished.
challenge.q: Why are the porters, singers, and Levites mentioned after the wall was completed?

answers: It helped identify the returnees and their family connections
It was used only for songs
It determined the opening hours of the gates
challenge.explanation: The register recorded the ancestry of those who had returned from captivity.
challenge.q: How did the genealogical register support the organization of Jerusalem?

paragraphs.title: The Returnees and the Families of the People

easy.explanation: The returnees are introduced as those who came with Zerubbabel and the other leaders.
easy.q: With whom did the list of returnees begin?

easy.explanation: The passage records families, numbers of people, and groups identified by cities.
easy.q: What is described in this list?

easy.explanation: The children of Parosh numbered two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
easy.q: How many were listed as the children of Parosh?

medium.q: Which family was larger according to the numbers given: the children of Shephatiah or the children of Arah?

answers: Those who climbed onto the wall
Those who went up to the top of a mountain
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the people who returned from Babylonian captivity.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “went up out of the captivity” describe?

answers: Families are listed first, followed by groups identified by cities
Animals are listed first, followed by priests
Offerings are listed first, followed by gates
medium.explanation: The passage first names families and then identifies several groups by their cities.
medium.q: How is this part of the list arranged?

answers: The returnees were identified by family and by place
Only city residents belonged to the people
challenge.explanation: The list uses both ancestry and place of origin to identify the returnees.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the fact that both families and cities are mentioned?

challenge.explanation: The children of Hariph numbered one hundred twelve.
challenge.q: Which group listed in these verses numbered 112?

answers: The men of Kirjath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth
challenge.explanation: The group from Kirjath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth numbered 743.
challenge.q: Which city group was the largest among those listed through verse 38?

easy.explanation: The list begins with the priests.
easy.q: Which group appears first in this section?

easy.explanation: The children of Asaph numbered one hundred forty-eight.
easy.q: How many were listed among the singers, the children of Asaph?

easy.explanation: The porters numbered one hundred thirty-eight.
easy.q: How many were listed among the porters?

medium.explanation: The children of Asaph are specifically identified as singers.
medium.q: Which group was especially associated with singing?

medium.explanation: Porters were responsible for duties connected with the gates.

medium.q: Which group was smaller: the Levites or the singers?

answers: The record distinguishes the general population from religious and communal roles
All the officials were members of the royal family
The roles replaced the family groups
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from general families to priests, Levites, singers, and porters.
challenge.q: What is the significance of moving from the families of the people to this list?

challenge.explanation: The Levites numbered 74, exactly half of the singers’ 148.
challenge.q: Which group numbered exactly half as many as the singers?

answers: The porters served at the gates and the singers served through music
challenge.explanation: Their names indicate different responsibilities: guarding gates and singing.
challenge.q: Why were the porters and singers different communal roles?

paragraphs.title: The Temple Servants and Solomon’s Servants

easy.explanation: The passage lists the families of the Nethinims and the children of Solomon’s servants.
easy.q: Which groups are listed in this section?

easy.explanation: The total number of the Nethinims and Solomon’s servants was 392.
easy.q: What is given at the end of this list?

easy.explanation: The children of Ziha are included among the Nethinims.
easy.q: Which family is named among the Nethinims?

medium.explanation: The Nethinims were a group associated with service at the sanctuary.
medium.q: What were the Nethinims associated with?

answers: As a long list of families
By the names of enemy cities
By the names of musical instruments
medium.explanation: The verses name many families of the Nethinims.
medium.q: How is the list of the Nethinims presented?

answers: They were connected with Israel and sanctuary service
They were commanders of the army
medium.explanation: Both groups are included among those connected with Israel’s community and service.
medium.q: What do the Nethinims and Solomon’s servants have in common in this passage?

answers: To summarize the size of the group
To state the number of gates
challenge.explanation: The total gives a summary of the detailed list.
challenge.q: Why is a total given after the individual families are listed?

answers: The group included many distinct families
The group had no connection with the community
challenge.explanation: The many names show that the group consisted of numerous families.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the length of the family list?

answers: The distinction between the Nethinims and Solomon’s servants
The distinction between priests and Levites
The distinction between cities and gates
challenge.explanation: The passage names the Nethinims and Solomon’s servants as related but distinct groups.
challenge.q: What distinction is preserved in the wording of this section?

paragraphs.title: Uncertain Ancestry and Restrictions on the Priesthood

answers: Their father’s house and their seed
The hours for opening the gates
easy.explanation: They could not show their father’s house or their ancestry.
easy.q: What could some of the returnees not show?

answers: They were put from the priesthood
easy.explanation: They were treated as polluted and removed from the priesthood.
easy.q: What happened to the priestly families whose register was not found?

easy.explanation: They were not to eat of the most holy things until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim.
easy.q: What were they forbidden to eat until the matter was resolved?

medium.explanation: The register was a genealogical record used to verify family descent.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy” refer to?

answers: A priest with Urim and Thummim had to stand
A new wall had to be built
The seventh month had to arrive
medium.explanation: The Tirshatha required them to wait until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim.
medium.q: What was required before the disputed families could eat the most holy things?

answers: Their priestly ancestry could not be proven
They did not know how to sing
They did not live in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Their genealogical record was not found, so their priestly descent remained unverified.
medium.q: Why were certain people restricted from the priesthood?

answers: Priestly questions required an authoritative determination
challenge.explanation: The decision was postponed until an authorized priest could make the matter clear.
challenge.q: What does the decision to wait for Urim and Thummim indicate?

answers: Uncertain ancestry led to restriction from priestly service until verification
Uncertain ancestry led to immediate appointment
challenge.explanation: Those whose ancestry could not be proven were not allowed to serve as priests until the issue was resolved.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between uncertain ancestry and exclusion from the priesthood?

answers: He was called after his wife’s family name
challenge.explanation: Barzillai had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called after their name.
challenge.q: What detail explains the difficulty concerning Barzillai’s ancestry?

easy.explanation: The whole congregation numbered forty-two thousand three hundred sixty.
easy.q: How many people were in the whole congregation together?

easy.explanation: The passage records two hundred forty-five singing men and singing women.
easy.q: How many singing men and singing women were mentioned?

easy.explanation: The groups dwelt in their cities when the seventh month came.
easy.q: Where did the priests, Levites, and the other groups dwell at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: The passage also gives numbers for servants, singers, horses, mules, camels, and asses.
medium.q: What was recorded in addition to the number of people?

answers: The name of a musical instrument
medium.explanation: The Tirshatha was the governing official who gave to the treasure and issued the priestly ruling.
medium.q: What was the Tirshatha in this passage?

answers: They supported the work and its treasury
medium.explanation: The gifts of gold, silver, and priestly garments were given for the work and its treasury.
medium.q: What purpose did the recorded contributions serve?

answers: The passage records support for the work and then the people dwelling in their cities
The contributions were made only after the cities were abandoned
The passage gives no sequence at all
challenge.explanation: The passage first records gifts for the work and concludes with the people living in their cities.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the contributions and the settlement in the cities?
Which animal was mentioned in the greater number?

answers: The community had settled in its cities
The wall had not yet been built
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends by saying that the people were dwelling in their cities when the seventh month came.
challenge.q: What does the ending of the chapter emphasize when the seventh month came?
